findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering used by audit logs
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor() returns cursor.value unchanged. The audit-log endpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so the key is a datetime: math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError when build_cursor() computes next/prev cursors, causing a 500 on the first optimized page. Even if that did not crash, returning the raw millisecond cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime like DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor() would make build_queryset() compare a datetime column against an integer. The optimized audit-log path is therefore unusable.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch crashes because Django querysets reject negative slicing
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and a client supplies a cursor with a negative offset, this branch executes list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with start_offset < 0 (and stop may also be <= 0). The comment claims the Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically, but Django QuerySet slicing explicitly raises AssertionError: "Negative indexing is not supported." A privileged audit-log user can craft e.g. a cursor with offset -1 and turn the request into a 500 instead of getting the claimed reverse-pagination behavior.

findings.title: BasePaginator change still allows negative offsets for previous-page cursors on every endpoint
findings.body: The new line clamps the offset only when cursor.is_prev is false: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. Cursor values are client-controlled (parsed from the cursor query parameter), so any user of any BasePaginator/DateTimePaginator/Paginator endpoint can supply a negative offset with is_prev=1 and still reach queryset[negative:stop], which Django rejects with AssertionError. This ungated change to the shared paginator does not fix the negative-index crash it appears to address and leaves a trivially triggerable 500 across all endpoints using these paginators, not just the admin-gated audit-log path.

findings.title: Unconditional dereference of organization_context.member can crash non-optimized requests
findings.body: enable_advanced is computed for every request as request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access, even when optimized_pagination is not requested. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional (None when the caller has no membership record for the organization), and because of the unconditional evaluation before the branch, such a request raises AttributeError and returns 500 instead of serving the normal DateTimePaginator path. The member check should be guarded (e.g. member is not None) and ideally only evaluated when use_optimized is true.

findings.title: New OptimizedCursorPaginator and endpoint branch have no test coverage
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class, modifies shared BasePaginator slicing, changes Cursor documentation to endorse negative offsets, and adds a new query-param/permission-gated branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but includes no tests. A single test exercising OptimizedCursorPaginator with the endpoint's actual -datetime ordering, plus tests for negative, zero, and previous-page cursors, would have caught the datetime TypeError and Django negative-slicing AssertionError described above before merge.
